summary: Ruth came home with a huge basket of barley and told Naomi about Boaz. Naomi was amazed and praised God, because Boaz was a close relative who could help them.

story_reel.narration: At the end of the day, Ruth beat out the barley she had gathered. It came to about an ephah, which is enough to fill a big basket! She carried it all home and also gave Naomi the leftover lunch Boaz had shared. Naomi's eyes went wide. 'Where did you work today? Blessed be the man who noticed you!' Ruth said, 'The man's name is Boaz.' Naomi gasped. 'May Yahweh bless him! Yahweh has not stopped showing His kindness to the living and the dead! That man is our close relative. He is one of our family redeemers.' A family redeemer was a relative who could rescue a family in trouble by buying back their land or caring for them. For the first time in a long time, Naomi had hope! She had called herself 'Mara,' bitter. But now she was praising God's kindness. Ruth kept working in Boaz's fields until the end of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest, and she lived with Naomi. Ruth's hard work and Boaz's kindness brought hope back to Naomi's heart. Our kindness can help others see God's kindness.

micro_prayer.text: Yahweh, thank You for Your kindness that never stops. Help me bring hope to others through my kindness and hard work. Amen.

companion.message: I love watching Naomi's hope come back! God's kindness had been there all along, and Ruth's faithful love helped Naomi see it.
